questions.question: In the simplex method, what does a single pivot do to the basis of a canonical tableau?
options: It adds the entering variable and keeps all basic ones
It replaces every basic variable by a new set at once
It removes the leaving variable without adding another
It exchanges the leaving variable for the entering one

questions.question: In a simplex tableau, the entering variable $x_k$ and the leaving basic variable $s_r$ have been selected. Which entry is the pivot element?
options: The coefficient of $s_r$ in the objective row
The right-hand side of the row of $s_r$
The largest coefficient in the column of $x_k$
The coefficient of $x_k$ in the row of $s_r$

questions.question: During a simplex pivot, why is the pivot row divided by the pivot element first?
options: So that the entering variable has coefficient $1$ in that row
So that the right-hand side becomes $1$ in that row
So that every coefficient in that row becomes at most $1$
So that the leaving variable gets coefficient $0$ in that row

questions.question: After a pivot in which $x_2$ enters and $s_2$ leaves, all numbers of the tableau have been updated. What else must be changed in the tableau?
options: Nothing: the labels follow from the numbers alone
The objective row's label: it now belongs to $x_2$
The pivot row's label: it now belongs to $x_2$
Every row label, since all basic values changed

questions.question: In a simplex pivot, multiples of the normalized pivot row are subtracted from other rows. Which rows must be updated in this way?
options: Only the constraint rows, not the objective row
Every other row, including the objective row
Only the rows with a positive entry in the pivot column
Only the objective row, as constraints keep their form

questions.question: For $\max\ 5x_1+2x_2$, the initial tableau has rows $z-5x_1-2x_2=0$, $4x_1+2x_2+s_1=12$ (basic $s_1$) and $x_1+3x_2+s_2=9$ (basic $s_2$); $x_1$ enters and the row of $s_1$ is the pivot row. What is the pivot row after dividing by the pivot element?

For $\max\ 5x_1+2x_2$, the initial tableau has rows $z-5x_1-2x_2=0$, $4x_1+2x_2+s_1=12$ (basic $s_1$) and $x_1+3x_2+s_2=9$ (basic $s_2$); $x_1$ enters and the row of $s_1$ is the pivot row. After the pivot row becomes $x_1+\frac{1}{2}x_2+\frac{1}{4}s_1=3$, what does the row of $s_2$ become?

For $\max\ 5x_1+2x_2$, the objective row $z-5x_1-2x_2=0$ must lose its $x_1$ term, because $x_1$ has entered the basis in the row that now reads $x_1+\frac{1}{2}x_2+\frac{1}{4}s_1=3$. What is the updated objective row?

For $\max\ 5x_1+2x_2$ with slacks $s_1,s_2$, a pivot produced the rows $z+\frac{1}{2}x_2+\frac{5}{4}s_1=15$, $x_1+\frac{1}{2}x_2+\frac{1}{4}s_1=3$ (basic $x_1$) and $\frac{5}{2}x_2-\frac{1}{4}s_1+s_2=6$ (basic $s_2$). What is the new basic solution?
A pivot divides one row by a nonzero number and adds multiples of it to the other rows of a tableau. What happens to the set of points satisfying the constraint equations?
options: It shrinks to the new basic solution only
It is unchanged; only its description changes
It grows, since the leaving variable is dropped
It changes, but the optimal point stays the same

questions.question: In a feasible canonical tableau, why does the simplex method pivot on the row chosen by the minimum-ratio rule, with a positive pivot element?
options: It is the only way to make the pivot column a unit column
It is the only way to update the objective row
It guarantees that every right-hand side stays nonnegative
It is the only way to make the leaving variable nonbasic

questions.question: Geometrically, for a two-variable LP, where does one simplex pivot from a corner of the feasible region lead?
options: Directly to the optimal corner, whatever the start
To an interior point of the feasible region
To an adjacent corner, along one edge of the region
To the corner opposite the current one, across the region

questions.question: A tableau has rows $z-x_1-4x_2=0$, $x_1+2x_2+s_1=10$ (basic $s_1$), $-x_1+x_2+s_2=2$ (basic $s_2$) and $3x_1-x_2+s_3=6$ (basic $s_3$). $x_2$ enters and the row of $s_2$ is the pivot row. What is the objective value after the pivot?

A tableau has rows $z-x_1-4x_2=0$, $x_1+2x_2+s_1=10$ (basic $s_1$), $-x_1+x_2+s_2=2$ (basic $s_2$) and $3x_1-x_2+s_3=6$ (basic $s_3$). $x_2$ enters and the row of $s_2$ is the pivot row. What is the right-hand side of the row of $s_3$ after the pivot?

A tableau has rows $z-x_1-4x_2=0$, $x_1+2x_2+s_1=10$ (basic $s_1$), $-x_1+x_2+s_2=2$ (basic $s_2$) and $3x_1-x_2+s_3=6$ (basic $s_3$). $x_2$ enters and the row of $s_2$ is the pivot row. After the pivot, which entries does the column of the leaving variable $s_2$ have in the rows $z$, $s_1$, $x_2$, $s_3$?

A tableau has rows $z-x_1-4x_2=0$, $x_1+2x_2+s_1=10$ (basic $s_1$), $-x_1+x_2+s_2=2$ (basic $s_2$) and $3x_1-x_2+s_3=6$ (basic $s_3$). $x_2$ enters. A student pivots on the entry $-1$ in the row of $s_3$. What does this produce?
options: A valid feasible tableau, as any nonzero element can be a pivot
$x_2=-6$: a basic solution that is not feasible
No tableau, as a negative element cannot be divided by
The same tableau as pivoting on the row of $s_2$

questions.question: After a pivot in which $x_2$ entered and $s_2$ left from the row $r$, a student pivots again in row $r$, now on the entry of $s_2$. What tableau results?
options: The previous tableau, with $s_2$ basic again in row $r$
A new tableau with neither $x_2$ nor $s_2$ basic
The previous tableau, but with all signs reversed
The previous tableau only if the pivot element was $1$

questions.question: A tableau has rows $z-x_1-4x_2=0$, $x_1+2x_2+s_1=10$ (basic $s_1$), $-x_1+x_2+s_2=2$ (basic $s_2$) and $3x_1-x_2+s_3=6$ (basic $s_3$). $x_2$ enters. A student pivots on the row of $s_1$ instead of the minimum-ratio row. What is then the right-hand side of the row of $s_2$?

For $\max\ 2x_1+5x_2$ with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the initial basis is $s_1,s_2,s_3$. After one pivot the rows are $z-\frac{3}{4}x_1+\frac{5}{4}s_2=15$, $\frac{1}{2}x_1+s_1-\frac{1}{2}s_2=2$, $\frac{1}{4}x_1+x_2+\frac{1}{4}s_2=3$, $x_1+s_3=5$. What was the pivot element of this pivot, as an entry of the initial tableau?
